title: Emptying desk sharpeners and punches
audience: Cleaners who service small office equipment during a waste route.
learningOutcomes: Empty a pencil sharpener's receptacle and clear its cutters without damaging the unit.
Empty and wipe a hole punch and return it to service.
Report equipment that will not clear rather than forcing it.

instruction.heading: Why small office equipment needs its own step
instruction.body: Desk sharpeners and punches gather shavings and punched dots, which jam the mechanism and spill onto desks. Empty them as you pass during the route rather than waiting for a complaint. Where a unit has a plug, unplug it before you touch the cutters or the receptacle.

instruction.heading: Pencil sharpeners
instruction.body: Unplug the sharpener first. Lift it over the bin, take out the receptacle and tip the shavings into the bin. If the cutters are clogged, wipe the blades using a dry cloth. Material lodged in the grooves can be picked out with a blunt tool, for example a bent paper clip. Keep oils, greases and abrasive products away from the mechanism, and never soak the unit in water. Refit the receptacle, return the sharpener to its place, plug it in and test it.

instruction.heading: Hole punches
instruction.body: Take the receptacle off the base and tip the dots into the bin. Wipe dust from the body using a dry, lint-free cloth; fit the receptacle back and set the punch in its usual place. Test it with a sheet of scrap paper if the site allows.

procedure: Unplug the unit if it has a plug.
Empty the receptacle into the collection bin.
Wipe the cutters using a dry cloth; clear lodged material with a blunt tool if needed.
Refit the receptacle and return the unit to its place.
Plug the sharpener back in and test it, or confirm the punch works.

workedExamples.situation: A sharpener at a reception desk has stopped cutting, and its receptacle is packed with shavings.
workedExamples.reasoning: Unplug the unit, empty the receptacle, check the cutters for lodged material, and clear them using a dry cloth and a blunt tool. Refit, return and test. If it still will not cut, report it to the site contact rather than forcing the mechanism.

equipmentAndPpe: Dry cloths, including a lint-free cloth
Blunt tool, for example a bent paper clip

commonErrors.error: Cleaning a sharpener while it is still plugged in.
Using oil or a cleaning spray on the cutters.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a dry cloth on the cutters only.

commonErrors.error: Forcing a stuck part until it breaks.
commonErrors.prevention: Report the fault to the site contact if it will not clear.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Unplug equipment before cleaning or clearing it.
Keep fingers away from cutter blades and keep the sharpener out of water.

qualityStandard: The receptacle is empty and refitted.
The cutters are clear of lodged material.
The unit is back in its place and has been tested.
documentationEvidence: Equipment faults reported to the site contact, with location.
summary: Unplug first, then empty the receptacle over the collection bin.
Use a dry cloth on the cutters; do not use oil, grease or abrasives.
Report equipment that will not clear rather than forcing it.
